newsitem.title: JAPAN: TENNIS-JAPAN'S DATE TO RETIRE IN NOVEMBER--REPORTS.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-JAPAN'S DATE TO RETIRE IN NOVEMBER--REPORTS.

text.p: Japan's top female tennis player Kimiko Date will give up her career in November when the current season ends, Japanese media reported on Tuesday.

Ranked seventh in the latest Women's Tennis Association rankings, Date defeated world champion Steffi Graf during the Federation Cup in April but was defeated by Graf in the Wimbledon semifinals in July.
Date, 25, has been one of the few Japanese to rise in the world of professional tennis and her success has made her a household name at home with a number of national product endorsements.
She turned professional in 1989 after ranking in the top four in the All Japan Championship in 1987.
Date became the first Japanese woman in 21 years to reach the Grand Slam semifinals in the 1994 Australian Open and to enter the top 10 world rankings.
A spokesman refused to confirm the news reports but said Date would hold a news conference later on Tuesday.
